title: Pho Bo
subtitle: Vietnamese beef noodle soup with charred ginger and spice
excerpt: A fragrant beef broth made with charred ginger and onion, star anise, cinnamon, and cloves, served over rice noodles with thin-sliced brisket. This simplified version develops real depth without needing 6 hours on the hob.
sourceNotes: Pho is believed to have originated in northern Vietnam in the early 20th century, likely influenced by both French pot-au-feu and Chinese beef noodle soups. It became a national dish eaten at all hours, particularly popular as a breakfast in Hanoi before spreading south with regional variations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The broth can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated. Skim any fat from the surface before reheating.

content.text: Charring the ginger and onion directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill before adding them to the broth is the step that gives pho its characteristic smokiness. Do not skip it.

items.prepNote: wide, soaked according to packet instructions

content.text: Char the ginger and onion halves by holding them directly over a gas flame with tongs or placing them under a very hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes per side until blackened on the cut surfaces. Brush off any loose char.

Put the brisket, beef stock, charred ginger, charred onion, star anise, cinnamon, and cloves in the stockpot. Bring to a boil, skimming any scum that rises. Reduce to a very gentle simmer and cook for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes until the brisket is very tender.
Lift out the brisket and set aside to cool slightly. Strain the broth through a sieve and discard the solids. Return the broth to the pan, season with salt, and keep at a gentle simmer.
Slice the brisket thinly against the grain. Drain the soaked noodles and divide between four deep bowls. Lay the sliced brisket over the noodles.
Ladle the hot broth over each bowl and top with spring onion, coriander, sliced chilli, and a wedge of lime. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Boiled too hard rather than simmered
items.fix: Keep the broth at the gentlest simmer throughout.
Char the ginger and onion until deeply coloured before adding to the pot.
Give it a full 90 minutes at a gentle simmer.
